source: 2019 AHA/ASA Guidelines for Acute Ischemic Stroke

recommendations.text: Stroke systems should prioritize rapid neurologic assessment and immediate brain imaging to determine reperfusion eligibility.

For Stroke Initial Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - activate stroke team - obtain last known well time - perform nihss - check glucose (within 10 minutes) - establish iv access - order stat ct head (within 25 minutes) - order cbc bmp coag - obtain 12 lead ecg
During Stroke Initial Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay ct for labs.
IV alteplase is recommended for eligible patients presenting within the treatment window after exclusion of contraindications.
For Tpa Eligibility Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - review inclusion criteria - review exclusion criteria - calculate time from onset - review anticoagulation status
tPA with BP >185/110 increases risk of intracranial hemorrhage. [FORBIDDEN: give_alteplase, give_tpa] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA/ASA 2019 Acute Ischemic Stroke Guidelines, Section 3.5

recommendations.text: Seizure at onset may indicate stroke mimic. tPA without exclusion is harmful. [FORBIDDEN: give_alteplase_without_ruling_out_mimic, give_tpa_for_todds_paralysis] (Severity: HIGH)
Posterior circulation strokes may have low NIHSS but devastating outcomes. [FORBIDDEN: discharge_with_low_nihss, withhold_treatment_based_on_low_nihss] (Severity: HIGH)
Anticoagulation within 24h of tPA increases hemorrhagic transformation risk. [FORBIDDEN: give_heparin_within_24h_of_tpa, start_doac_immediately] (Severity: CRITICAL)
IV tPA contraindicated beyond 4.5h window. [FORBIDDEN: give_alteplase] (Severity: CRITICAL)
When relative contraindications exist, treatment should follow individualized risk-benefit discussion and documented shared decision-making.
For Tpa Risk Benefit Discussion, the following actions are mandatory: - discuss with patient family - document shared decision
Eligible patients should receive IV alteplase promptly, followed by protocolized monitoring and avoidance of early antithrombotic therapy.

For Administer Iv Tpa, the following actions are mandatory: - obtain informed consent - give alteplase 0.9mg kg (within 60 minutes) - admit to icu or stroke unit - monitor bp q15min x2h then q30min x6h - neurological checks q15min - hold antiplatelet anticoagulation 24h

During Administer Iv Tpa, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give antiplatelet within 24h, give anticoagulation within 24h, give heparin within 24h, place foley within 30min, place ng tube within 30min, place arterial line within 30min.
After alteplase, frequent neurologic and blood pressure monitoring is required, with follow-up imaging before starting antithrombotics.
For Post Tpa Monitoring, the following actions are mandatory: - neurological monitoring - bp management target 180 105 - repeat ct 24h - start antiplatelet after 24h if no hemorrhage
During Post Tpa Monitoring, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give antiplatelet before 24h, give anticoagulation before 24h.
Patients with large-vessel occlusion should be screened for thrombectomy based on time, imaging profile, and functional baseline.
For Thrombectomy Eligibility, the following actions are mandatory: - confirm lvo on imaging - assess aspects score - calculate time from onset - assess prestroke mrs
Mechanical thrombectomy is strongly recommended for eligible large-vessel occlusion strokes in the early treatment window.

For Perform Thrombectomy, the following actions are mandatory: - activate neurointerventional team - obtain informed consent - perform thrombectomy procedure (within 60 minutes) - achieve tici 2b or better
Selected patients with favorable perfusion mismatch can benefit from thrombectomy up to 24 hours from last known well.
For Extended Window Thrombectomy, the following actions are mandatory: - confirm favorable perfusion imaging - perform thrombectomy procedure
After thrombectomy, intensive monitoring and blood pressure control are essential to reduce complications and optimize recovery.
For Post Thrombectomy Care, the following actions are mandatory: - admit to icu - neurological monitoring - bp management - groin site monitoring
Patients not receiving reperfusion should receive stroke-unit care, early antiplatelet therapy, and complication prevention measures.
recommendations.source_section: Acute Ischemic Stroke Care Without Reperfusion

recommendations.text: For Non Reperfusion Management, the following actions are mandatory: - admit to stroke unit - aspirin within 24 48h - dvt prophylaxis - swallow screen - early mobilization
recommendations.source_section: Acute Ischemic Stroke Care Without Reperfusion

recommendations.text: During Non Reperfusion Management, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give anticoagulation for stroke prevention in first 24h.
recommendations.source_section: Acute Ischemic Stroke Care Without Reperfusion

recommendations.text: Blood pressure must be reduced below 185/110 mmHg before alteplase and maintained below 180/105 mmHg afterward.
recommendations.source_section: Blood Pressure Targets for Thrombolysis Candidates

recommendations.text: For Bp Management Tpa Candidate, the following actions are mandatory: - reduce bp to below 185 110 before tpa - use iv labetalol or nicardipine - maintain bp below 180 105 post tpa
recommendations.source_section: Blood Pressure Targets for Thrombolysis Candidates

recommendations.text: During Bp Management Tpa Candidate, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give tpa if bp uncontrolled.
recommendations.source_section: Blood Pressure Targets for Thrombolysis Candidates

recommendations.text: In patients not receiving thrombolysis, permissive hypertension is acceptable unless blood pressure is markedly elevated.
For Bp Management Non Tpa, the following actions are mandatory: - treat if bp above 220 120 - goal reduction 15 percent
Hemorrhagic stroke management includes urgent reversal of coagulopathy, blood pressure control, and neurosurgical evaluation.

For Hemorrhagic Stroke Management, the following actions are mandatory: - admit to icu - bp reduction target 140 - reverse anticoagulation if applicable (within 60 minutes) - neurosurgery consult - repeat ct 6h or if deterioration
During Hemorrhagic Stroke Management, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give tpa, give antiplatelet, give anticoagulation.
FFP alone is insufficient for warfarin reversal in ICH. PCC preferred. [FORBIDDEN: give_ffp_as_sole_reversal, delay_reversal_for_inr_result] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA/ASA 2022 ICH Guidelines, Section 5.2; Steiner T, Stroke 2016

recommendations.text: Surgical intervention should be considered for selected intracerebral hemorrhage patients with mass effect or hydrocephalus.
For Neurosurgical Intervention, the following actions are mandatory: - neurosurgery evaluation - consider evacuation if indicated - evd for hydrocephalus
For non-surgical ICH, guideline-based conservative care focuses on physiologic optimization and prevention of secondary injury.
For Ich Conservative Management, the following actions are mandatory: - bp management - icp monitoring if indicated - seizure prophylaxis consideration - dvt prophylaxis mechanical
Sudden deterioration after thrombolysis requires immediate neuroimaging and coagulation assessment for hemorrhagic transformation.
For Hemorrhagic Transformation Evaluation, the following actions are mandatory: - stop tpa infusion - stat ct head (within 15 minutes) - stat coagulation panel - type and screen
Confirmed hemorrhagic transformation should prompt rapid reversal strategies, intensive care, and neurosurgical consultation.
For Hemorrhagic Transformation Management, the following actions are mandatory: - give cryoprecipitate - give tranexamic acid - reverse coagulopathy - neurosurgery consult - icu management
Neurologic worsening after stroke requires urgent reassessment for edema, hemorrhage, or recurrent ischemia.
For Stroke Deterioration Evaluation, the following actions are mandatory: - repeat nihss - stat ct head - evaluate for recurrent stroke - evaluate for hemorrhage - evaluate for edema
Malignant edema management includes early neurocritical care measures and decompressive surgery consideration when indicated.
For Malignant Edema Management, the following actions are mandatory: - elevate head of bed - avoid hyperthermia - avoid hyperglycemia - neurosurgery consult for decompressive craniectomy
Comprehensive secondary prevention should include antithrombotic therapy, risk-factor control, and etiology-directed interventions.

For Stroke Secondary Prevention, the following actions are mandatory: - antiplatelet therapy - statin therapy - bp management long term - diabetes management - smoking cessation - carotid evaluation - cardiac monitoring for afib
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and nitroprusside are teratogenic. [FORBIDDEN: give_ace_inhibitor, give_arb, give_nitroprusside] (Severity: CRITICAL)
In AF-related stroke, anticoagulation is recommended after individualized timing assessment to reduce recurrent embolic events.
For Afib Anticoagulation, the following actions are mandatory: - calculate chadsvasc - calculate hasbled - start doac preferred
During Afib Anticoagulation, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: start anticoagulation before 24h post tpa.
Symptomatic carotid stenosis should be evaluated for timely revascularization based on stenosis severity and procedural risk.
For Carotid Intervention Evaluation, the following actions are mandatory: - confirm stenosis degree - assess surgical risk
Carotid endarterectomy is recommended for appropriate symptomatic high-grade stenosis when performed within a favorable timeframe.
For Carotid Endarterectomy, the following actions are mandatory: - surgical planning - perform cea within 2 weeks
Carotid stenting is a reasonable alternative in selected patients with symptomatic stenosis and elevated surgical risk.
For Carotid Stenting, the following actions are mandatory: - dual antiplatelet before procedure - perform cas
Early multidisciplinary rehabilitation and structured discharge planning improve functional outcomes after stroke.
For Stroke Rehabilitation, the following actions are mandatory: - early rehabilitation assessment - physical therapy - occupational therapy - speech therapy if needed - discharge planning
